extracted.intended_audience: top-rank junior researchers from abroad considering applying for the Sofja Kovalevskaja Award (to head a research group in Germany)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/administrative rules for applicants seeking the Sofja Kovalevskaja Award — a five-year grant (up to €1.65M) to establish and lead a research group in Germany. Covers eligibility, required documents, host requirements, use of funds, selection procedure and post-award conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target applicant profile / award purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Award for top-rank junior researchers from abroad to spend five years building up a working group and working on a high-profile, innovative research project of their own choice at a research institution of their own choice in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program closed to new applications after 2020; funding for last winners expires 2026. Applicants should be successful top-rank junior researchers and plan to lead a working group in Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctorate timing (eligibility window)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply only if you completed your doctorate with distinction in the last six years (calculated to the application deadline). In case of several doctorates, the effective date is that of the first doctoral degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relevant date is the date of completing the final academic part (e.g., defence). If you obtained your doctorate more than six years ago, exceptions may be made in well-founded cases (e.g., parental leave) — contact info@avh.de with CV and publication list for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate eligibility when a PhD is not customary
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is not customary or possible to take a doctorate in your country/discipline, you can apply if you prove academic performance equivalent to a PhD (e.g., publications in internationally reviewed journals/publishing houses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case you may apply up to 10 years after your first degree (B.A., M.A., etc.). Send complete CV (without gaps) and list of publications before applying for advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician (MD/Dr. med.) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Physicians are eligible if they hold a research doctorate or comparable academic degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the 'Admission questionnaire for physicians (MD / Dr. med.)' for detailed information. If multiple research doctorates apply, the 'several doctorates' rule applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career breaks allowance (parental leave and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods of interrupted academic career for child-rearing, military/alternative service, care of relatives, or long-term illness may be taken into account to extend the eligibility window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mothers can claim two extra years for each child born after their PhD plus other verifiable parenting periods; fathers/other carers credited only with verifiable parenting periods. The overall extension is limited to 6 years. Job hunting, unemployment and non-academic employment do NOT count as career breaks. Contact info@avh.de for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence/work location requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be living and/or working outside Germany at the time of application; aim is to enable highly qualified academics from abroad to launch a career in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If already in Germany or recently been to Germany, you may only apply if you have spent a total of over 12 months within the 18 months immediately preceding the application deadline outside Germany. German citizens/educational residents are generally ineligible if they have been in Germany within the last 18 months prior to deadline or are already in Germany, unless permanently working abroad (see detailed conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rule for German citizens / educational residents
rubrics_metrics.description: German citizens and/or educational residents are generally ineligible unless they are permanently working abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered permanently established abroad if: living/working abroad >10 years; or >5 years plus one of: permanent/tenured position, additional citizenship of country of residence, permanent residence permit, or other indications of intent to remain. If in doubt, send CV and publication list to info@avh.de.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual exclusivity with Humboldt Fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot apply to the Sofja Kovalevskaja Award programme and the Humboldt Foundation's Fellowship Programme at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you fulfil the formal requirements, you must choose one application path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language proficiency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural sciences and engineering: good knowledge of German or English is sufficient. Humanities/social sciences: knowledge of German if necessary for the project (language certificate required). Physicians: good German required if work with patients; otherwise English sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Native speakers or those long resident in English- or German-speaking countries do not need to submit a language certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic host selection and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: You are free to choose your own academic host (person who will act as the award winner’s direct academic contact, e.g., chair holder or head of department). Applications involving return to the supervisor of the doctoral thesis or to the mentor of a longer postdoc stay are generally rejected for lack of academic independence, unless scientifically justified and elucidated in the research outline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have already worked in Germany for a longer period (12 months or more) you should look for a new academic environment. The Foundation does not provide direct host-finding support but lists search engines and databases. Discuss the position form and income conditions with the host while preparing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single host institution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to carry out research at two different research institutions; the award winner must use the award funds to carry out the approved research outline at the host institution presented in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions for changing the host institution during the sponsorship period are in principle not provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Only complete applications can be submitted; once the review process by independent reviewers has been initiated it is not possible to submit or exchange documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper is accepted after application submission, send acceptance letter immediately by email to be fed into the process prior to the selection meeting. It is not possible to add to the publication list once the procedure has started. The application deadline is stated in the Programme information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert reviews: quantity, content, age and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit two expert reviews (the host’s statement does not count as an expert review). Expert reviews should assess your development as a researcher, your potential, and academic accomplishments; they should be provided by reviewers well acquainted with your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert reviews should not be more than 12 months old at time of application. Only two expert reviews will be considered; additional ones cannot be taken into account. Host and reviewers upload documents themselves using secure links from the application form. You are responsible for ensuring documents are complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key publications requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Your application must contain five key publications that demonstrate your previous outstanding achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should choose works that present your most important academic results and, in cases of multiple authorship, those to which you made a major contribution. When choosing, include works reflecting more recent publication activity. You should explain the academic relevance of each key publication and indicate personal contribution for multi-author works. Key publications must also appear in the complete list of publications. You cannot amend your selection of key publications once the selection process has begun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted publication status for cited works
rubrics_metrics.description: You may only cite publications that are already in print, have been accepted for publication, or have at least been submitted to a publishing house (with proof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted to a publisher, include acknowledgement of receipt; if accepted, include letter of acceptance. Any other works cited will be deleted. Exception: your dissertation may be cited as a key publication even if not yet submitted for printing (upload original manuscript). Unpublished dissertation may not be listed in the complete list of publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research outline and financial plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a research outline and a financial plan; information and samples are in the application form and sample financial plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The financial plan will be examined in an independent specialist review and by the selection committee to ascertain whether the itemisation is plausible and appropriate; their assessment will determine the award amount. Provide as detailed fund request information as possible to help budgetary planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award period constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The award funds support a five-year sponsorship period; it is not possible to apply for a period in excess of five years. Applications for a significantly shorter period (less than about four and a half years) have no chance of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The research stay commences in the calendar year in which the award is granted; exact start date should be agreed with the host prior to application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on accepting positions during selection
rubrics_metrics.description: If you accept a leadership position in Germany or a permanent employment contract in Germany before the selection meeting (or while selection procedure is underway), your application becomes ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is intended to enable first leadership positions in Germany for those without substantial ties to Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection procedure and decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are reviewed by independent peer reviewers; the final decision is made by the Selection Committee consisting of researchers of all disciplines, deciding by a two-thirds majority vote. The Humboldt Foundation has no vote on the Selection Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection Committee typically meets at the end of March; applicants are informed immediately afterwards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success rate / award numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to six awards are expected in a given year; recent selection rounds showed a probability of success of approximately 10%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets realistic expectations for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel funding / duplicate funding rule
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible in principle to apply to another institution for funding at the same time, but you must state this on the application form and inform the Foundation immediately about any parallel applications and decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must indicate third-party funding (granted or applied for) in the 'Information on the financial plan'. Double funding (duplicating financing for the same research project) is forbidden. Additional funds for closely related subprojects require strict division of budgets and clear documentation; violations may lead to reclaiming of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and administration of award funds (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Award funds may be used for project costs, personnel (including drawing a personal income), administrative flat-rate, equipment, invitations to academics (travel, accommodation, meals, remuneration), group outings, interviewing costs, language courses if necessary, and certain small expenses (mobile phone, local transport, meals) subject to host institution rules and Regulations on the Use of Funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any equipment purchased becomes the property of the host institution at project end. Cash balance as per Dec 31 must not exceed 20% of the total instalment paid that year (exceptions possible). Funds must be spent by the end of the sponsorship period; remaining funds remitted to the Foundation. Travel expenses claimed according to host institution regulations. Discuss small 'ready cash' provision with host administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative flat-rate rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative flat-rate is paid to the host institution; the basis for calculating it is the original amount of award funds (excluding interest accrued).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which section of the host institution receives it should be clarified with the host institution and cited in the agreement. The administrative flat-rate may be used for entertaining academic guests and similar administrative expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff employment and fellowship awarding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment of staff should follow the legal framework of the host institution; all typical forms are possible (TVöD/TV-L, fee agreements, fellowships). The host institution acts as employer on the award winner's behalf and is entitled to grant fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award winner may earmark funds for the host to use for fellowships. Fellowship rates should be based on DAAD/Humboldt specified rates; deviations are possible if convincingly justified and documented. The Foundation recommends an ad hoc committee for selecting fellows. The host institution must carry out the administrative act of granting fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation responsibilities and presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Award winners are responsible for their taxation. The Foundation assumes the award will be classified as a grant toward a research project in Germany and, as such, be free of tax; whether the portion for living expenses is taxable should be examined individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing double taxation agreements and laws in award winners’ countries may be relevant. For fellowships funded from award funds, attention to special tax regulations is needed. For detailed tax questions obtain advice from a tax advisor or host institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement / equipment acquisition guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment and scientific supplies may be purchased abroad and brought to Germany if necessary for the project's success; purchases must respect the Regulations on the Use of Funds and host procurement rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement procedures should be economical and prudent, but time-sensitive needs and international competition may justify urgent procurement without full tendering under applicable procurement law provisions (example cited: § 3 Nr. 4 lit f) VOL/A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property / patents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is registered in the framework of the award, the Foundation does not claim any share in the patent; the 'German Employees Invention Act' applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation should be informed if a patent is registered. Award funds may be used to cover patent registration costs if covered under the Regulations on the Use of Funds (cf. VII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Foundation logo and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications and other public presentations deriving from projects sponsored by the award should make appropriate reference to sponsorship by the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and the BMBF; use of the Foundation logo is subject to strict rules and requires prior written authorisation except for downloadable 'Unterstützt von/Supported by' logo from 'My Humboldt' for direct sponsorship outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The logo is a trademarked inseparable word/image mark and may not be altered. Any other use requires prior written permission stating intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash-management restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The cash balance as per December 31 must not exceed 20% of the total instalment paid that year (can be exceeded in exceptional cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments are made in instalments according to the financial plan and effected as soon as possible depending on demand and budget availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and notification obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: You must inform the Foundation of applications for or receipt of (partial) funding from German or foreign sources and observe general obligations of award winners (e.g., fully focusing work on the funded research project in Germany).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forbidden to duplicate financing for the same research project. Contacts within host administration will advise on congruent funding issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising positions guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements for positions (fellowships, jobs) should conform to host institution legal frameworks and, where appropriate, make reference to sponsorship by the Foundation and the BMBF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on target group, ads may be placed worldwide (e.g., EURAXESS Jobs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship taxation note (host-administered fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships granted by the host institution in the framework of the award should follow Humboldt Fellowship regulations and are assumed to be free of tax in Germany according to § 3 No. 44 of German Income Tax Law (subject to concrete case criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institution handles granting; further information should be obtained from host/institutional administration or tax office where needed.
